title: The Concept of Social Capital
text:
Social capital refers to the value derived from social networks and relationships within a community. It encompasses the trust, norms, and mutual obligations that facilitate cooperation and collective action without requiring formal institutions.

This form of capital is distinct from economic or human capital because it rests on shared connections rather than tangible assets. High levels of social capital are often correlated with increased civic engagement, better public health outcomes, and greater resilience during times of crisis.

The maintenance and development of social capital require active participation and the establishment of reliable social structures, such as community groups or reliable institutional trust.
